text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent midweek newspapers on Wednesday. These are the last editions of the two newspapers for this year. Publication resumes on January 8.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Botswana government has not yet finalised its position on Namibia's proposal to draw water from the Okavango River. A recent Namibian delegation seems to have come to Botswana, not to debate the issue, but rather to dictate what will happen.
- The Opposition Botswana National Front welcomes 803 converts from the ruling Botswana Democratic Party in the constituency of Mahalapye, a few kilometres from the capital, Gaborone.
- The Kgalagadi (Kalahari) South areas of Botswnaa has been declared drought-stricken and the government has provided two million pula in relief.

- The Ministry of Agriculture confirms that Botswana is buying cattle from Namibia and South Africa to restock Ngamiland, where 300,000 head were killed as part of an exercise to eradicate cattle lung disease. Two thousand head have been bought from Namibia and an undisclosed number from South Africa. A total of 60,000 head is required. The cost of the exercise so far is estimated at 157.9 million pula.

- President Masire is photographed in one of an undisclosed number of F5 fighter aircraft delivered to the Botswana Defence Force (BDF). The planes have been bought from Canada. They were shown to the President, cabinet ministers and some members of the local press last Friday at Sir Seretse Khama International Airport. Earlier stories from June this year indicated that 13 aircraft would be purchased for 150 million pula.
